items.text: Thank you for your order. Unfortunately, the item you requested is out of stock. We will ship it as soon as it becomes available.

analysis.translation: ご注文ありがとうございます。あいにく、ご希望の商品は在庫切れです。入荷しだい発送いたします。

slash.en: Thank you for your order.
slash.ja: ご注文ありがとうございます

slash.en: Unfortunately, the item you requested is out of stock.
slash.ja: あいにく、ご希望の商品は在庫切れです

slash.en: We will ship it as soon as it becomes available.
slash.ja: 入荷しだい発送します

pattern.explanation: the item (S) is (V) out of stock (C)。you requested が the item を修飾しています。

clauses.text: Thank you for your order. Unfortunately, the item you requested is out of stock. We will ship it as soon as it becomes available.

elements.note: 省略された関係代名詞を含む主語

tense.name: 現在形・未来形
tense.explanation: 状態は現在形、これからの対応は will ship で述べます。

grammar.explanation: 「~しだい」。接続詞なので後ろに主語と動詞が続きます。

grammar.point: 目的格の関係代名詞の省略
grammar.explanation: the item (that) you requested。
「在庫切れ」

vocab.toeic: The item is out of stock.
文頭で悪い知らせを導く

points.detail: as soon as(接続詞)と as long as・even though などの区別

paraphrase: We will send it right after it arrives.

phrases.t: We will ship it as soon as it becomes available.

iu.t: Thank you for your order.
Unfortunately, the item you requested is out of stock.
We will ship it as soon as it becomes available.

quiz.question: Thank you for your order. Unfortunately, the item you requested is out of stock. We will ship it ______ it becomes available.
quiz.explanation: 「入荷しだい」は as soon as。as long as は「~である限り」、even though は「~だけれども」、in case は「~に備えて」で文意に合いません。

items.text: The parking lot will be closed for repairs next week. Employees are asked to use the public garage across the street. We apologize for any inconvenience.

analysis.translation: 駐車場は来週、補修のため閉鎖されます。従業員の皆様は、通りの向かいの公共駐車場をご利用ください。ご不便をおかけして申し訳ありません。

slash.en: The parking lot will be closed for repairs next week.
slash.ja: 駐車場は来週補修のため閉鎖されます

slash.en: Employees are asked to use the public garage across the street.
slash.ja: 従業員は通りの向かいの公共駐車場の利用を求められています

slash.en: We apologize for any inconvenience.
slash.ja: ご不便をおかけして申し訳ありません

pattern.explanation: The parking lot (S) will be closed (V)。for repairs が閉鎖の理由を表します。

clauses.text: The parking lot will be closed for repairs next week. Employees are asked to use the public garage across the street. We apologize for any inconvenience.

tense.name: 未来の受動態・現在形の受動態
tense.explanation: 閉鎖は will be closed、依頼は are asked to ~ で、行為者を出さずに伝えます。

grammar.explanation: 「~するよう求められている」。お知らせ文で依頼を丁寧に伝える形。
「~をお詫びする」。for の後ろは名詞。
「~の向かいに」

points.detail: apologize for と across の用法

paraphrase: Staff members should park in the public garage.
We are sorry for the trouble.

phrases.t: to use the public garage across the street.

iu.t: The parking lot will be closed for repairs next week.
Employees are asked to use the public garage across the street.
We apologize for any inconvenience.

quiz.question: The parking lot will be closed for repairs next week. Employees ______ to use the public garage across the street. We apologize for any inconvenience.
quiz.explanation: 従業員は「求められる」側なので受動態 are asked が正解。ask や have asked は、従業員が主語だと意味が合いません。asking は are の後で能動の進行形になってしまいます。

items.text: Our company is moving to a new office on June 1. All staff members must pack their belongings by May 30. Therefore, no meetings will be scheduled during that week.

analysis.translation: 当社は6月1日に新しいオフィスへ移転します。社員全員は5月30日までに私物を荷造りしてください。そのため、その週は会議を入れません。

slash.en: Our company is moving to a new office on June 1.
slash.ja: 当社は6月1日に新オフィスへ移転します

slash.en: All staff members must pack their belongings by May 30.
slash.ja: 社員全員が5月30日までに私物を荷造りしなければなりません

slash.en: Therefore, no meetings will be scheduled during that week.
slash.ja: そのため、その週は会議を予定しません

pattern.explanation: Our company (S) is moving (V)。to ~ は移転先、on June 1 は日付です。

clauses.text: Our company is moving to a new office on June 1. All staff members must pack their belongings by May 30. Therefore, no meetings will be scheduled during that week.

elements.note: 近い予定を表す現在進行形

tense.name: 現在進行形・助動詞・未来の受動態
tense.explanation: 予定は現在進行形、義務は must、結果は will be scheduled で述べます。

grammar.explanation: 前の内容の結果を導く。前文との論理関係(原因→結果)で選ぶ。
by は期限、during は期間を表す。
「1つも~ない」という強い否定。

points.detail: Therefore / However / Otherwise の使い分け

paraphrase: As a result, there will be no meetings that week.
Staff must finish packing before May 30.

phrases.t: to a new office on June 1.
All staff members must pack their belongings by May 30.
no meetings will be scheduled during that week.

iu.t: Our company is moving to a new office on June 1.
All staff members must pack their belongings by May 30.
Therefore, no meetings will be scheduled during that week.

quiz.question: Our company is moving to a new office on June 1. All staff members must pack their belongings by May 30. ______ no meetings will be scheduled during that week.
quiz.explanation: 前の文(移転作業で忙しくなる)の結果として「会議を入れない」と述べているので Therefore が正解。However は逆接、Otherwise は「さもなければ」、Meanwhile は「その間に」で、論理がつながりません。

items.text: I am writing to inform you about a change in our return policy. Customers can now return items within sixty days of purchase. This new policy takes effect on March 1.

analysis.translation: 返品規定の変更についてお知らせします。お客様は購入後60日以内であれば商品を返品できるようになりました。この新しい規定は3月1日に発効します。

slash.en: I am writing to inform you about a change in our return policy.
slash.ja: 返品規定の変更についてお知らせします

slash.en: Customers can now return items within sixty days of purchase.
slash.ja: お客様は購入から60日以内に商品を返品できます

slash.en: This new policy takes effect on March 1.
slash.ja: この新規定は3月1日に発効します

pattern.explanation: I (S) am writing (V)。to inform you about ~ が手紙を書く目的を表します。

clauses.text: I am writing to inform you about a change in our return policy. Customers can now return items within sixty days of purchase. This new policy takes effect on March 1.

elements.text: about a change in our return policy

tense.name: 現在進行形・助動詞 can・現在形
tense.explanation: 目的は I am writing to ~、可能は can、発効は takes effect で述べます。

grammar.explanation: メールの冒頭の定型。目的を述べる。
「~以内に」。期間の上限を表す。
「(規則などが)発効する」

points.detail: within(以内)と during・while の区別

paraphrase: The new rule starts on March 1.
Items can be returned up to sixty days after buying.

phrases.t: I am writing to inform you
about a change in our return policy.
This new policy takes effect on March 1.

iu.t: I am writing to inform you about a change in our return policy.
Customers can now return items within sixty days of purchase.
This new policy takes effect on March 1.

quiz.question: I am writing to inform you about a change in our return policy. Customers can now return items ______ sixty days of purchase. This new policy takes effect on March 1.
quiz.explanation: 「購入から60日以内に」と期間の上限を表すのは within。during は特定の期間の「間」を表し、while は接続詞、among は「~の間で(3つ以上)」で、意味が合いません。

items.text: Brighton Hotel is looking for a front desk clerk. Applicants should have at least two years of experience in customer service. Interested candidates should send their resumes to the personnel office.

analysis.translation: ブライトン・ホテルは、フロント係を募集しています。応募者は、接客の経験が少なくとも2年必要です。ご関心のある方は、人事部に履歴書を送ってください。

slash.en: Brighton Hotel is looking for a front desk clerk.
slash.ja: ブライトン・ホテルはフロント係を募集しています

slash.en: Applicants should have at least two years of experience in customer service.
slash.ja: 応募者は接客の経験が少なくとも2年必要です

slash.en: Interested candidates should send their resumes to the personnel office.
slash.ja: 関心のある方は人事部に履歴書を送ってください

pattern.explanation: Brighton Hotel (S) is looking for (V) a front desk clerk (O)。look for は「探す」の意味の群動詞です。

clauses.text: Brighton Hotel is looking for a front desk clerk. Applicants should have at least two years of experience in customer service. Interested candidates should send their resumes to the personnel office.

tense.name: 現在進行形・助動詞 should
tense.explanation: 募集中は現在進行形、応募条件と手順は should で述べます。

grammar.explanation: 感情を表す分詞は、人が主語のとき過去分詞形。「興味を持っている応募者」。
「少なくとも」
「~を探す、募集する」

paraphrase: Those who are interested should e-mail their resumes.
The hotel needs someone for its reception.

phrases.t: Applicants should have at least two years of experience in customer service.
should send their resumes to the personnel office.

iu.t: Brighton Hotel is looking for a front desk clerk.
Applicants should have at least two years of experience in customer service.
Interested candidates should send their resumes to the personnel office.

quiz.question: Brighton Hotel is looking for a front desk clerk. Applicants should have at least two years of experience in customer service. ______ candidates should send their resumes to the personnel office.
quiz.explanation: 「関心を持っている応募者」は、人の気持ちを表す過去分詞の形容詞 Interested。Interesting は「(物事が)興味深い」、Interest は名詞/動詞、Interestingly は副詞で candidates を修飾できません。

items.text: The annual company picnic will be held on Saturday, July 12. All employees must register online before June 30. Those who do not register will not be able to attend.

analysis.translation: 毎年恒例の会社のピクニックは、7月12日の土曜日に開かれます。従業員は全員、6月30日までにオンラインで登録しなければなりません。登録しなかった人は、参加できません。

slash.en: The annual company picnic will be held on Saturday, July 12.
slash.ja: 毎年恒例の会社のピクニックは7月12日(土)に開かれます

slash.en: All employees must register online before June 30.
slash.ja: 従業員は全員6月30日までにオンライン登録が必要です

slash.en: Those who do not register will not be able to attend.
slash.ja: 登録しない人は参加できません

pattern.explanation: The annual company picnic (S) will be held (V)。行事の開催を受動態で述べる定番の形です。

clauses.text: The annual company picnic will be held on Saturday, July 12. All employees must register online before June 30. Those who do not register will not be able to attend.

tense.name: 未来の受動態・助動詞
tense.explanation: 開催は will be held、義務は must、結果は will not be able to ~ で述べます。

grammar.explanation: 「~しなければならない」。続く文(登録しないと参加できない)から、義務だと判断できる。
「~する人々」。関係代名詞 who を使った言い方。
can の未来形・否定形として使う。

points.detail: must / might / would の選び方(後続文との整合)

paraphrase: Everyone has to sign up on the Internet by June 30.
People who skip registration cannot join.

phrases.t: All employees must register online before June 30.
will not be able to attend.

iu.t: The annual company picnic will be held on Saturday, July 12.
All employees must register online before June 30.
Those who do not register will not be able to attend.

quiz.question: The annual company picnic will be held on Saturday, July 12. All employees ______ register online before June 30. Those who do not register will not be able to attend.
quiz.explanation: 次の文で「登録しない人は参加できない」とあるので、登録は義務の must が正解。might は「かもしれない」で弱すぎ、used to は過去の習慣、would be は動詞の原形 register に続けられません。

items.text: Ms. Alvarez joined our company in 2018. She is the manager who oversees the Chicago branch. Under her leadership, sales have increased by twenty percent.

analysis.translation: アルバレスさんは2018年に当社に入社しました。彼女はシカゴ支店を統括する部長です。彼女のリーダーシップのもと、売り上げは20%増加しました。

slash.en: Ms. Alvarez joined our company in 2018.
slash.ja: アルバレスさんは2018年に入社しました

slash.en: She is the manager who oversees the Chicago branch.
slash.ja: 彼女はシカゴ支店を統括する部長です

slash.en: Under her leadership, sales have increased by twenty percent.
slash.ja: 彼女の指導のもと、売り上げは20%増えました

pattern.explanation: She (S) is (V) the manager who oversees ... (C)。who 以下が the manager を修飾します。

clauses.text: Ms. Alvarez joined our company in 2018. She is the manager who oversees the Chicago branch. Under her leadership, sales have increased by twenty percent.

elements.text: the manager who oversees the Chicago branch

tense.name: 過去形・現在形・現在完了
tense.explanation: 入社は過去形、現在の役割は現在形、成果は現在完了 have increased で述べます。

grammar.point: 主格の関係代名詞 who
grammar.explanation: 先行詞が人(the manager)で、関係詞節の主語になるとき who を使う。
増加の差を表す。by twenty percent = 20%分。
「彼女の指導のもとで」

points.detail: who / which / whose / whom の選び方
現在完了で成果を述べる

paraphrase: She is in charge of the Chicago branch.
Sales rose by twenty percent while she was leading it.

phrases.t: Ms. Alvarez joined our company in 2018.
sales have increased by twenty percent.

iu.t: Ms. Alvarez joined our company in 2018.
She is the manager who oversees the Chicago branch.
Under her leadership, sales have increased by twenty percent.

quiz.question: Ms. Alvarez joined our company in 2018. She is the manager ______ oversees the Chicago branch. Under her leadership, sales have increased by twenty percent.
quiz.explanation: 先行詞 the manager は人で、関係詞節の中で主語(oversees の主語)になるので、主格の who が正解。which は物、whose は所有格、whom は目的格です。

items.text: Our new software is much faster than the old version. It also uses less memory. As a result, employees can finish their work more quickly.

analysis.translation: 新しいソフトウェアは、旧バージョンよりずっと速くなっています。使用するメモリも少なくなりました。その結果、従業員はより早く仕事を終えられます。

slash.en: Our new software is much faster than the old version.
slash.ja: 新しいソフトは旧バージョンよりずっと速いです

slash.en: It also uses less memory.
slash.ja: 使うメモリも少なくなりました

slash.en: As a result, employees can finish their work more quickly.
slash.ja: その結果、従業員はより早く仕事を終えられます

pattern.explanation: Our new software (S) is (V) much faster than the old version (C)。比較級 faster に than が対応します。

clauses.text: Our new software is much faster than the old version. It also uses less memory. As a result, employees can finish their work more quickly.

elements.text: much faster than the old version

tense.name: 現在形
tense.explanation: 性能の比較と現在の状態を現在形で述べます。

grammar.explanation: faster than ~ のように、比較級の後ろには than が来る。
比較級を強める言い方。very では強調できない。
「その結果」。前の内容の結果を表す。

points.detail: 比較級と than の対応
As a result が結果を導く

paraphrase: The latest program runs a lot quicker than the previous one.

phrases.t: employees can finish their work more quickly.

iu.t: Our new software is much faster than the old version.
It also uses less memory.
As a result, employees can finish their work more quickly.

quiz.question: Our new software is much faster ______ the old version. It also uses less memory. As a result, employees can finish their work more quickly.
quiz.explanation: 比較級 faster の後ろで比べる対象を導くのは than。that・as・then では比較の文になりません(as は as ~ as の形で使います)。
